request.spec:

every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).

request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).
A change of the sheet's today that puts a claim past its due-by, or takes one out of overdue, is
such a change even when no due or due-total moved.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The change is in and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What changed:** only `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/Rollup.java`.
- The rollup now works out each person's overdue-total the same way the screen does: their counted claims that are overdue, with the late charge, skipping n/a. It also adds these up into the sheet's overdue-total.
- A person gets a `ROLLUP` line when their claimed, due-total or overdue-total moved. Each line now ends with `overdue-total=<x>`.
- A `TOTALS` line is written when any of the three totals moved. It now ends with `overdue-total=<total>`.

**Changes of the sheet's today:** changing today already took the rollup before and after the change and wrote what moved. So moving today so that a claim becomes overdue, or stops being overdue, now writes the lines even when no due or due-total changed. The server and front end needed no other changes.
